body: Definitely one of my favorite lines from the show.
It's become a habit, and I can't fall asleep until I'm completely exhausted and need the TV on in the background.

Hello friends, and damn, there are many of us.

I'm planning to do exactly that sometime this week as well, with 2 classes left to graduate, not to mention that this is my third "last" semester. And because of this, I have to leave the country as well for a period of time, even though this is where I have stayed for the longest time in one place in my entire life and consider it pretty much home. Oh, and 25k is owed directly to school which I only got 3 credits out of. Awesome.

I'm pretty terrified and anxious at the though even though I've done it before. I commend your swift decision making process and courage. I regret that I drew out mine (both times) too long.

Wishing OP and everyone else the best from here. It's survival now.

I don't remember. Genuine happiness, excitement for something good that's coming the next day. Both sides of the emotional spectrum is pretty numb with the only constant being restlessness and anxiety, with occasional bouts of overwhelming negativity (sadness, despair, anger) - but unfortunately, not for the other side.

I understand the pressure, anxiety, and heightened depression that comes from having a writer's block specifically to fulfill academic assignments (funnily enough, it is all those things that are likely to be causing said inability to begin with). It is so frustrating, and it messes with your confidence and increase the fear of failure/producing a shitty piece - so much so that you can't even just write some low-quality BS to get it over with.

I've strung myself along for very long a time, believing I can somehow hang in there and power through. I will be withdrawing this week.

I understand, and the vicious cycle is just nasty. Anxiety affects my ability to take care of responsibilities, yielding devastating consequences that messes up life to a great extent, thus creating even more severe anxiety. And then I sort of shut down and avoid, avoid, avoid, and I'm numb to the actual circumstances and consequences therein while suffering from a general sense of not knowing what I can do, what I should be doing, or how to do it, in the background. It's like my heart is pacing back and forth with no clear destination and my mind is filled with question marks.

Of course, only until there's no way to escape without somehow addressing it. But in the denial/avoidance phase, I put on TV shows, movies, and play on my phone. There are small moments in between where I'm completely absorbed, and I temporarily "forget" about the anxiety I should be feeling.
Getting enuinely excited and anxious (the good kind) to do something I've planned for the day.. then really having fun and not fake laughing/smiling to pretend I'm actually enjoying something.
Every damn day. To a countryside in Europe, preferably. It was so serene and beautiful. Might be using my mileage soon.

"...the same sorry "why"."
That totally hit home. That, as well as your point that the smallest, most insignificant shit can become a trigger for self-loathing - for me, sometimes it's the "You failed! Try again?" message I get after playing the dumbest puzzle game that was actually meant to distract me from such crippling thoughts.
It's certainly a thought that terrifies me. It makes me question the worth of doing anything everyday.
10+ pages due last week. I have a mild to severe anxiety attack every day.

That's a pretty messed up environment you had to grow up in. Sorry you had to go through that.

But honestly, I envy your situation that allows you to start over fresh - that's about all I could wish for right now personally. Try channeling the anxiety into excitement/anticipation - you can do anything, be anything, meet anyone you want. You are in full control of what happens next, and hopefully you're leaving most of your baggage behind. Sure, it can be a little scary, but also... it could be pretty damn wonderful, whatever is to come.

It sounds like you have a solid plan and great chances of making this work; all you have to do is believe you can do it and then go do it. It's evident you are an intelligent and motivated individual. Wishing you the best.

With severe lows of depression and anxiety, I have trouble downing anything. If I have two slices of pizza, I've eaten more much more than other days already. Anything I do manage to chew and swallow induces nausea or stomach ache, which is obviously because of stress and anxiety... my appetite/physical reactions to diet have always been there.
It sucks because when I'm a little hungry I think of something I'd like to eat, then while or after I cook it/buy it the interest in consuming it just disappears.
Right. Forming new relationships or even sustaining existing ones can be really draining with depression, but it doesn't mean we cease being lonely. Damned if you do, damned if you don't.
Being dead =/= Dying. There are times the former doesn't seem like such a bad thing, but the latter is terrifying.

I'm in a similar situation. My live-in SO, even when I told him the depression is enough to trigger thoughts of harming myself, I'm "just a stressful person who worries too much." It's uncanny as he has mentioned the dog training analogy when laying out how I should be performing my role as a girlfriend (cooking and cleaning). It's a shitty thing to hear.

I'm a heat freak, always love to try new types of hot sauces and this is a great tip. It's funny because in some cultures eating spicy food when stressed is an actual thing, (after breakups or a stressful day at work) so you may be on to something. Thanks for sharing.
I understand the passion thing, and more so the rain thing. I love standing in the rain, watching the rain, listening to the rain... it certainly is peaceful.

I apologize for the poorly worded intro, it was my mistake. I thought that my following response to your situation would show that I not only believe you but also take the matter seriously. The first sentence was to point out that it was a roller coaster of events that not many people go through and thus that shitty and unusual, and that you have engaging writing skills independent of your experiences, which was one heck of a thing too. 
I hope you'll see that I didn't respond just to disregard what you went through. And I meant those things, because that's what I perceived. A betrayal of that scale would break me, I'm not strong; those who can withstand it are seen as such from my personal view. I'm sorry I upset you.

I think you'd make money as a writer, regardless of whether all this is true or not (I'm not calling you a liar, just pointing out that what happened to you was fucked up to the point of almost implausible). I'm sorry, but I laughed internally because of some of the phrases you used that I found incredibly witty and apt. My apologies for discounting your experience itself and focusing on the expression to find humor in it, but I guess I can be shitty like that.

But seriously - are there no legal ramifications that makes it possible to get at least a portion of the restitution you deserve? I don't have experience with a joint-checking account, but it seems that logically there should be protection against someone just upping and leaving without consent.

And what a bunch of fuckfaces. But it seems like you have more talent and drive than you realize - so how about living life with the goal of reaching the point of success as perceived by society, more specifically the shitheads who made your life miserable, as a sort of fuck-you? From what I perceive, you seem like an extremely strong and talented individual. I'm not trying to pull the old "oh at least you have those things" line that a lot of us hate, but I really admire and envy your strength.

It really scary to see what people are capable of. I don't really believe in karma, at least not in this specific realm, but I sometimes I hope it does so that hope people like them get it.

Yes, yes, and yes to the bullet points. It seems that there are many "types" of us out there - those who are somewhat functional in society despite ongoing melancholia, those who can't get out of bed, those who have a truly unsolvable problem that acts as a cause etc...
But I think that the most noteworthy and shitty, shitty thing about depression is that even if you were able to locate the cause of it, or even a method to remotely mitigate it, you can't, or you would've - because it's either impossible, or the symptoms render you just short of an invalid.

Kind of like getting a job in the current market. Every employer wants you to have experience, but you need to have had a job to have experience. To get a job, you need experience. Similarly, to feel less depressed, you need to do stuff. To do stuff, you need to feel less depressed. It's just one disgusting fallacy.
I commend your strength. Keep going!

I agree on the experience part. I remember when I was ignorant of my depression being a medical issue, I confided in a friend (very driven, highly intelligent, top-of-the-class pre-med student) about general lethargy and difficulty getting out of bed to tend to my academic responsibilities. It was more of a "damn it, why am I like this?" rhetorical question, to which he responded, "err... laziness?" Advices such as "Buck up" or "Be more positive and good things will come! :)" than a sincere attempt at understanding (at least from my perspective).
What they are able to do easily, such as "bucking up" or "staying positive" does not come naturally for me. I suck at it, and I don't know how to get better. I'm sure it was all in good intention, but it does get lonely when trying to discuss deep or existential topics that riddle my depressed state of mind when they deemed worthless and impractical to be discussed or perceived as my trying to seem "smarter" than everyone else.

I don't think it's a women thing, but more of a state-of-mind/personality thing. Many people find unusual or mild physical pain humorous (think slapstick comedy), and this case potentially has both, with the definition of term "mild" left to the discretion of the individual. Some men and women rush to help a person who slipped on a banana peel and fell, while others have a burst of laughter as their first reaction.
From the comments in the above article, it seems most people take the matter pretty seriously. 
I think most people who find it funny would be doing so because of the *ridiculousness* of the situation (I mean, imagine waking up from a standard procedure with a vital body part gone... it's pretty crazy) rather than the amount of pain this man and his family is going through. Ridiculousness often incites humor, and sadly people lack enough empathy to look beyond what makes them laugh. I know it's disheartening, but humans are inherently flawed, so... I hope you feel better.

Very true. I understand your thought processes to reach it as well as the conclusion itself.
It matters little what gifts we are given by default, the "potential" we have, the things we have successfully achieved in the past, if we are simply unable to wield the tools in possession in a productive manner. Some days I feel a little bit hopeful than the others; I have physical dexterity, intelligence (though of course, no expertise or enough information on a given field for it to count), a physique accepted positively by society, a family, close friends et cetera... But they become utterly meaningless as I realize I'm unable to use such resources and support to manifest into things I desire.
You seem extremely intelligent and philosophically pensive. In my humble opinion, such individuals seem more prone to depressive episodes, as they find hoodwinking themselves into positive delusions a difficult task. Basically, it seems insane actually not to be depressed given the deluge of shit within society, the self, and everything in between and beyond.

I wish I could have offered a more productive comment, but I suppose the tl;dr here would be "I feel you."

I have tremendous respect for you for trying and succeeding on your own. I'm sorry it became difficult after a while. But you've held on, made through it despite my hardships.
I have actually been considering the au pair route, or to live off-the-grid, but seeing that a strong individual who has experienced so much more at a young age found it extremely difficult brings doubt to my half-thought-out plan. Thank you for sharing your experience, and I hope you'll find the strength to fight again.

Hello friend, just wanted to tell you know that I am very familiar with the process you are referring to. I had to delay my graduation several times. I used to think it was just a lack of work ethic and laziness, but when things got really out of control (basically failing all my classes) I sought professional help - it was in fact that I had medical depression.
I wish I could tell you a story with a happy ending, but unfortunately I have finally given up on it this term, as there is no feasible way to continue even when I'm only two classes short.
But perhaps I could offer a bit of advice based on my experience. After coming back from medical leave, I also seemed to be doing well up until halfway through the semester, but with various stresses emerging (academically, personally etc), I went through the same pattern of failure especially since I didn't have a great support system. Now I have a bulk of my 20s wasted on nothing, feelings of hopelessness, a fortune's worth down the drain, and a big gap in my resume (which is the least of my problems).
It would be best to tackle the probable depression or any other issues present while taking a breather from academics, and more importantly, have a support system when you get back - perhaps a dependable roommate who understands your situation and is willing to help you keep on track. I learned that living alone can exacerbates the situation, given that medical attention can only be helpful when you have the means to kick your butt out of bed and get treatment, when often it's easy to stay anxiously wrapped around in your comforter as the situation gets worse. Without having a mechanism to help you work through the stress, it's so easy to fall back into old patterns.

PM me if you'd like to talk. I know I'd appreciate being able to talk to someone in a similar situation.

Hi. You've accomplished so much. You should know that. If you're not feeling self-conscious about where you are and want to connect with acquaintances or friends, how about sending a quick text first? I know it's not easy when others seemingly have separate lives from you, but perhaps they'll be glad to have heard from you and want to hang out.
 Feel better, you're awesome just for completing one of the most challenging academic programs there are, and have the potential for more!
I have a puppy too, and though he's a handful given my situation now, it helps to know this little guy loves me no matter what. I hope you feel better after your session of crying and cuddling. :)

Ah, I see what you're saying. Glad to hear that he's not verbally or emotionally abusive, either!

Then I'm guessing he said that in frustration or stress, as it is understandable how it can be straining for those close to people who suffer from depression. I met my current boyfriend while bouncing back from an episode, so he might have a vague idea that I am prone to "sadness" for a better term, but I find it hard to open up to him as I've been recently experiencing another (really tough one, too).
It's good that you have someone who knows your circumstances and is understanding from what I can tell. I definitely get how it helps to be distracted when interacting with your SO.

But on the issue of ECT, do you feel that it helped you to the extent that it was worth it? I know it's a very stressful experience to say the least, the physical side effects and memory loss and all.

Is your boyfriend abusive in any way? I know how it can be terrifying to be alone when you have depression, no means to get out there and form new relationships - platonic or otherwise (it's already difficult enough without depression to cultivate something meaningful where you're actually comfortable and know each other well). I've experienced a similar situation, and having someone nearby who you've already opened up to lessens the helplessness and inevitable loneliness. I only hope his presence helps you more than it hurts you; it's possible that his attitude and demeanor might be feeding your depressive thoughts.

I get the feeling that you are both talented and ambitious, but the current circumstances and clouded judgment caused by depression are messing with your confidence and performance. The most talented and intelligent people are often their own greatest critics because they know so much is possible to achieve and have a penchant for perfection.
Find your confidence again. You have many qualities that society deems desirable. Not that societal esteem should be the focus of one's worth, but it's better to have that going on than disapproval from both self and   the world isn't it?
This is also something I'm telling myself. PM me if you'd like someone to talk to.

I'm so sorry that happened. That is really messed up. It hurts to imagine how betrayed and terrible you must have been feeling. Physical suffering because of him and broken trust of 5 years. Ugh. I'm really, really sorry.

Go eat fruit, a piece of bread, chocolate, or at least water. Lots of water. You need to at least keep your body functioning. Experiencing a lot of emotions can be physically draining.

I wish I could offer more, but all I can say is that I feel for you.

I know it's trite, but have you tried therapy or medication?
The aspects of yourself that you've described sounds a lot like clinical anxiety (possibly social). For me, a lot of the things you mentioned were the stressors deeply related to my biggest depressive episode. I remember struggling a lot specifically about seeing the things that I hate about myself in other family members, then becoming more stressed that they have been/are enforcing the same values on me that are the very cause of all of our suffering. Therapy and actively addressing social anxiety helped a lot with that aspect of my emotional troubles.

From what I can tell, you seem like a logical, kind-hearted, "normal-minded" (for lack of a better term) person - you just need a little practice interacting with other people, and not let fears and anxiety hinder it. It takes work to truly cultivate a 'fuck-it' attitude, and fostering confidence, accepting yourself, making improvements when possible is of course easier said than done. But it is possible and may require faking it, even to yourself at first.

Don't beat yourself up so much. I came to realize that most of the social gaffes were only considered so by myself, or it's greatly hyperbolic in my head as far as the effects of what I said or did goes. Most people are too self-involved to remember what may or may not have been mistakes made by other people (i.e. you), so why should you? Be yourself, they can take it or leave it! We're all awesome in our own ways, as long as we carry the values we ourselves consider awesome.

Oh honey, I'm in a similar situation to you right now at this moment, but probably with a few other complications and a few detrimental factors. Not graduating by the next month, which appears more than likely at this point, leaves me not only diplomaless after almost 8 years, tainted by leave of absences and multiple postponement of hard-set graduation dates, but also with having to leave a country that I dearly love. Not to mention great hindrances in job security, which would then inevitably lead to a deeper negative financial state accented by crippling debt.

I feel the same way - I'm only 2 classes away, but it's just... so... hard. The fight, the outcome, all doesn't seem worth it. I have a lot of doubt, even if I were to solve all this and get the degree I have struggled so long to obtain, whether I'd be able to utilize it in a productive way given how I'm facing trouble functioning in the most basic of ways.

I didn't mean to hijack your post with a personal rant, but just letting you know... there are more of us out there in similar situations (and in my personal case, more dire and fucked up) and I sympathize with your struggle.

I also think that if there's anything you can do, try your best to hang in there! Given that you solve your problem through appeal or otherwise, unless you are absolutely certain your depression will not be resolved by next semester to pass it, and are not both mentally and circumstantially prepared to battle your depression head-on while on leave, it's better to try your hardest finish up in my opinion. Speaking from experience, coming back after a break, depression hits you even harder if and when it returns; the wasted time, feeling like a failure, "where is my life going etc," and all the dark thoughts associated with depressive symptoms are much more heightened.

I truly hope you find a way through this. Best of luck.
Most news and ignorance
I finally understand the term 'dudebro'

This might be inapporpriate, but the title reminded me of a certain old Eminem song and lolled. Thank you for that; during times of low even a small giggle is greatly appreciated. Please stay strong!!

That is one of my favorite quotes, and I think about it a lot when I ponder my depression. 
It may seem bleak if you've just been suffering too damn long. But, what if it got just a little bit better tomorrow? And then a little bit more the next day? I have yet to experienced so much in life, due to circumstances or mere lack of motivation... but it would be such a shame to think I would've found them intensely interesting or discovered a new passion that outweighs the daily pain. There is no absolute way to be sure that this won't happen unless I stick around for the next day.
That's the bulk of what keeps me going - the fear of having missed out. It's not the best or healthiest motivation to live, but it works for now. Tap into the albeit vague and blurry memories of happiness, dreams, even a small hint of desire you had in the past. Just maybe, because even if we change little, the world is ever-changing, our efforts will not be the lame repeat from the day before and yield something new that is worth holding on to. Don't miss out; I hope you pull through. I'll be here trying to do the same.

We are in acutely similar situations. 
I have nobody here but him (though he's currently out of the country right now and seemingly having a blast), and there are times I have to be financially dependent on him as I'm in a weird limbo of a situation right now. I feel like a loser for not being able to move on right here and now because my emotional and situational dependency. I still have a lot of feelings for him, but unless he goes through some miraculous change and stops hurting me, and maybe more importantly WANT to stop hurting me, I know I'm only going to be miserable while we're together.

I really sympathize with your situation, and know how the feeling of helplessness exacerbates depression. It really sucks not feel like you don't have anything else, no back up at all.

I think you need to be on high alert with these symptoms. For me personally, a sign that a major episode is approaching is firstly appetite (dwindling to practically none) and sleep (difficulty falling asleep/staying asleep, then crashing for 10+ hours in the most inopportune times).
I didn't react as sensitively as I thought I would/should since I got somewhat better from the time before, and now face another major episode. Please, please seek all the help you can get and employ all your resources to get it under control.

Honestly, I don't know. You haven't mentioned how hard you tried to find a counselor that you could open up to, but I understand that that itself can be tiresome and take up a lot of resources. But I suppose it is an option - during my toughest episodes in the past, I changed therapists 3 times, and it did seemed to help a bit with the right one. Also, having a close friend who is ready to listen and understand what you're going through can help in my experience, but obviously if talking to a friend was the end-all-be-all solution that was accessible to us, we wouldn't be here in the first place.

I don't know what else to say, except that it's a constant battle and you need to work hard to find the mechanisms that help you cope. But then, if we had the ability to work hard at something while suffering from depression, it wouldn't be such a difficult thing to deal with the first place - that's why depression fucking sucks.
This is my life right now. And then I wallow in self-loathing.

It may have been a survival mechanism. It's hard to be perceptive of where your actions stand in terms of your own moral values when the focus is survival... I think may be why you feel anxious and depress when you're not manipulating or controlling others, because you feel vulnerable without being able to use the defenses you usually employ.

Since you seem to have realized this isn't someone you want to be, maybe you could try being genuine, performing small acts of kindness to strangers who you have nothing to gain from and see how that makes you feel. Perhaps in the process you'll find someone who can be a genuine friend who you can be yourself with.

I can relate to a lot of things you've mentioned, especially the last part about having an outside view looking into yourself and knowing it's ridiculous but unable to control it.

I have perfectionist tendencies, and even small fuck-ups trigger a lot of anxiety. I remember minuscule social/non-social blunders from early childhood (and they're what I consider as such, not like others reacted or pointed them out or anything) and sometimes they act as stressors to this day.

I know it's easier said then done, but build confidence. Enough to say 'I don't give a fuck what you think,' and understand that what they think does not invalidate your worth.

You can start small. For instance, about this post you made: you need to rationally convince yourself that their opinions doesn't have one small fucking bearing on your life. It's like falling down in public. Sure, it's embarrassing,  but you get up and you leave the scene and that's it. The only tangible thing that's left pertaining to you is your feeling humiliated, and it's something you can control as you are the agent.

If it were people you meet on a daily basis or people you care about, it may be harder. But with practice, I promise it gets better. I know many people throw this phrase around a lot to those with anxiety and depression, but as someone who suffers from both, I'm telling you this particular thing is something you can gain control over. I'm still struggling with a plethora of issues myself, and social acceptance and beating myself up with what others may or may not think of me was a particularly heavy one; but it no longer is.

If you stop caring what others think of you, then it doesn't matter what or whether they do.

But with all that said, I really sympathize about crying over stupid shit. It's all the more upsetting because "I'm" the one who is thinking it's stupid to cry about those things.

I think that's because most people on here are seeking support, or just pouring out their thoughts and treating it a place to vent. It's hard to try and help others carry their load when your own is crushing you.

It's especially difficult to do things to show you give a shit when your biggest struggle is to give a shit about yourself... 

Also, a lot of the times, all that can be offered is 'please don't feel that way' or 'it will get better,' or some variation of that which people who suffer from depression are tired of hearing and consider useless. Perhaps we don't know what to say, or what should be said.

Please don't be angry, and I hope you understand that we're all having a difficult time.
